newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt selling off more cement shares.
newsitem.headline: Egypt selling off more cement shares.

text.p: Egypt announced its biggest partial privatisation offer for weeks on Friday -- the sale of up to 4.2 million shares in Suez Cement with a market value of about 300 million pounds ($89 million).

The state's Holding Company for Mining and Refractories said the shares, currently owned by four partially privatised cement companies, would go on sale by public subscription to individuals, mutual funds and private-sector companies.
It said the companies were offering one million shares and could increase this to 4.2 million, about 8.5 percent of Suez Cement's total equity. It will announce further details soon.
It will be the biggest privatisation since at least early March, when the state sold about 3.5 million shares in cigarette manufacturer Eastern Company for over 300 million pounds.

All of the privatisation offers since then have been relatively small. The latest was of 350,000 shares in Development and Engineering Consultancy, worth about 11.5 million pounds. The offer closed on Wednesday but the agents have not yet indicated the level of public interest.
Cairo brokers say they are anxiously awaiting new privatisation offers to stimulate the market, which has stabilised after a sharp correction from record highs.
The big cement companies are a mainstay of the Egyptian stock market, often accounting for half of total turnover.

International securities house HSBC James Capel, in a detailed report on the sector in February, said two other cement companies -- Amriyah Cement and Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA -- were the most attractive cement stocks.
It calculated the discounted cash flow value of Suez Cement stock at 59.00 pounds a share. The shares closed on the Egyptian stock exchange on Thursday at 72.03 pounds.
The shares went through a successful flotation last year as global depositary receipts (GDRs) traded in London at a starting price of $14.75, equivalent to about 50 pounds.
The holding company said Suez Cement made net attributable profits of 190 million pounds ($56 million) in the first nine months of 1996, against 280 million in all of 1995.
The company's cement production in the whole of 1996 was 2.879 million tonnes, against 2.867 million tonnes in 1995, it added.
Net revenue from operations was 365 million pounds in the nine-month period, compared with 466 million in all 1995.

The holding company, which retains a stake in Suez Cement, said work was under way on a second line at the company's Suez plant to produce 1.35 million tonnes a year and on expanding the first production line by 215,000 tonnes a year.
These projects will increase the company's capacity to 4.3 million tonnes a year, it said. It did not say when the extra capacity would come on stream.
The nine-month profits are equivalent to 3.88 pounds for each of the 49 million shares.
